fields.meta_title: Patient Intake Form Builder for Medical Practices | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a patient intake form that collects insurance and health history online and flags gaps before the visit. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Patient Intake Form Patients Finish Before They Arrive
fields.hero_description: List the sections your clinic asks for and who should see which answers. Emergent builds the patient intake form people fill in on their phones, plus the database every answer lands in.
fields.features_heading: What the Online Version Adds to the Paper Packet
fields.features_subheading: Each one replaces a step your front desk does by hand once the clipboard comes back.
fields.feature_1:
Card photos with the plan details

Ask for a picture of the card's front and back on the screen where the plan is entered. Both images are saved to the patient's record beside the member ID and group number.
fields.feature_2:
Medications asked for by type

Split the medication question into prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal supplements. Patients add one row per item with the dose and how often they take it.
fields.feature_3:
History as a checklist

Turn the medical history page into conditions to tick, with a details box that opens only on a yes. Patients who have never had surgery skip every question about past operations.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts for answers that need a person

Alert the staff member who owns an answer by email or in Slack once it arrives. A plan outside the accepted list goes to billing; a referral sent without labs goes to scheduling.
fields.feature_5:
Signed office policies

Place the financial policy and the consent to treat after the last question and collect a typed or drawn signature. Each signed copy is stored with the answers from that visit.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, on your servers

Export the full code for the form and its database to your GitHub. A developer can host it on the practice's own servers or connect it to the scheduling software already in use.

fields.usecase_heading: Patient Intake for Four Kinds of Practice
fields.tab_content_1:
The billing lead sees an unaccepted plan two days early

Cedar Hollow Family Medicine asks each new patient to photograph both sides of the insurance card. The link goes out at booking and is due two days before the visit. A plan missing from the accepted list goes to Dana Price, the billing lead, the moment the form arrives. She calls in time to rebook or switch to self-pay.
fields.tab_content_2:
Referrals missing lab results wait in the coordinator's queue

Referred patients upload the referral letter and recent lab results to the Lakeside Endocrine intake, and name the doctor who sent them. A referral with no labs attached never reaches the booking calendar. Grace Obi, the referral coordinator, gets it instead, requests the results, and releases a slot once they arrive.
fields.tab_content_3:
One parent, two children, two patient records

Parents with more than one child fill in the Maple Pediatrics form once for the household, entering contact details and insurance a single time. Each child gets a page for allergies and the immunization record. Submitting creates a separate patient record per child, with the parent listed as guardian on each.
fields.tab_content_4:
Chest pain moves a walk-in to the top of the nurse's list

The QR code at the Riverbend Urgent Care front desk opens the intake on the patient's own phone. Patients give a reason for the visit and tick symptoms from a short list. Ticking chest pain or trouble breathing moves a patient to the top of the triage queue and alerts Kim Alvarez, the nurse on shift.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Patient Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work happens before you build anything: deciding what the clinician must know at the first visit, and which answers a person has to see early.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Gather the packet you use now
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the sections in visit order
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Mark the answers someone must see
fields.howto_step_1_des: Collect every page a new patient fills in today, including the ones handed over at the desk. Mark each question by who reads the answer: billing, the nurse, the clinician. Strike any question whose answer nobody on staff has looked at in a year.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with who the patient is and how to reach them. Insurance comes next, then health history. Leave the office policies for the end. Give each section its own screen, sized to read on a phone without zooming or scrolling sideways.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Patients leave out what they do not think of as medicine, such as a daily vitamin or an allergy spray. Give each category its own prompt and ask for the dose beside every entry. Put allergies on the same screen, each with the reaction it causes.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which answers need a person before the visit: an insurance plan you do not accept, a missing referral, a symptom the nurse wants flagged. Name one staff member for each, and choose whether they hear about it by email or in Slack.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your sections and rules into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the intake form and the database table its answers are saved to. Change a question or a rule later by prompting again, and the live form updates.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Put the policies and signatures last
fields.howto_step_6_des: Add the financial policy, the consent to treat and any notice your practice gives patients after the final question, each with a signature field. Have your practice manager or counsel confirm the wording before real patients sign it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as three made-up patients
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run one patient whose plan you accept, one whose plan you do not and one who triggers a symptom alert. Fill each in on a phone. Check that every alert reaches the right person and that the insurance photos open.

plan.angle: Seven of the top 10 are clinic PDFs (an endocrinology practice, primary care, a podiatrist, an ENT clinic, an OB/GYN service) plus a fill-and-sign library and one how-to. They all show the same sections: demographics, insurance, history, medications and allergies, reason for visit. This page names those sections and what to ask in each, then shows four practices where the online version does the front-desk work a PDF leaves behind: insurance checked before the visit, a referral packet complete on arrival, one parent registering two children, and a walk-in triaged from the waiting room.
